Oud is one of the most talked-about notes in perfume: deep, woody and a little smoky. Designer houses such as Tom Ford, Gucci, Guerlain and Chopard each have their own take on it. Here is what oud is, how the best-known oud perfumes differ, and how to choose and wear one.

What is oud?

Oud, also called agarwood or aoud, is a dark, fragrant resin that forms in the wood of agar (Aquilaria) trees. It has been treasured in the Middle East and South Asia for centuries, burned as incense and worn as an oil. Natural oud is rare, so many modern perfumes use an oud accord: a blend of woods, resins and leathery notes built to give the same rich effect. Gucci, for example, lists an oud accord in its base notes.

Tom Ford Oud Wood

Tom Ford Oud Wood Eau de Parfum (from £115.99, 30ml or 50ml) is the gentlest way into oud. Its key notes are oud wood, rosewood and cardamom over sandalwood, vetiver, tonka bean and amber, so the oud reads smooth and warm rather than smoky. It is unisex and easy to wear in the office or in the evening. See every Tom Ford fragrance, or read our Tom Ford perfume guide for Black Orchid, Noir Extreme and Neroli Portofino.

Gucci Intense Oud

Gucci Intense Oud Eau de Parfum (£73.99, 90ml) is darker. Black pepper and olibanum (frankincense) open it; amber woods, sandalwood and cedarwood sit at the heart; leather, patchouli, gurjun balsam and the oud accord form the base. Expect incense and leather more than sweetness. Shop all Gucci.

Tom Ford Oud Wood or Gucci Intense Oud?

  • Choose Oud Wood if you want a soft, creamy wood with a touch of spice that suits everyday wear.
  • Choose Intense Oud if you like incense, leather and a bolder, smokier trail for evenings and colder months.

Three more oud perfumes

  • Guerlain Oud Essentiel (£94.99, 125ml): saffron and pelargonium, then rose, oud and cedarwood over leather, frankincense and guaiac wood. A rose-and-leather oud, made unisex.
  • Chopard Oud Malaki (£48.99, 80ml): grapefruit, lavender and artemisia, then tobacco, spices and leather over oud, ambergris and dark woods. Made for men, and the most affordable oud in this guide.
  • Montale Aoud Damascus (£52.99, 100ml): damask rose, aoud and saffron with amber, woods and musk. Montale is known for rose and oud, and this one is made for women.

The Al Haramain Amber Oud editions

Al Haramain's Amber Oud range is a popular Arabian line, but read the notes: not every edition is built around oud. Amber Oud White Edition (from £34.99) is bergamot and orange, then jasmine, rose and freesia over musk, vanilla and patchouli, and is listed for women. Amber Oud Carbon Edition (from £35.99) is a fresh, aromatic men's scent of lavender, rosemary, bergamot, sage and vetiver. Amber Oud Bleu Edition (from £38.99) is citrus and mint over incense, vetiver and sandalwood. For the Gold, Ruby, Tobacco and Black editions, and for Lattafa, read our guide to Arabian perfume and Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa.

Which oud perfume suits you?

  • New to oud: Tom Ford Oud Wood, or a fresher Amber Oud edition.
  • You love incense and leather: Gucci Intense Oud or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • You love rose: Montale Aoud Damascus or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • Warm and spicy: Chopard Oud Malaki.

Oud is traditionally unisex, so "for men" or "for women" on the label is only a starting point. Browse unisex perfume, perfume for men and perfume for women.

How to wear oud

  1. Start small: one or two sprays. Oud notes are rich, and a little goes a long way.
  2. Apply to moisturised skin on the wrists, neck or chest. Our guide to layering oud with body butter explains why.
  3. Let it settle: do not rub your wrists together. Oud perfumes often change a lot after the first half hour, so judge them later in the day.
  4. Test before you buy a full bottle if you can, or start with a smaller size.

Good to know

  • Eau de parfum is the most common strength for oud perfumes; read extrait vs eau de parfum for what the label means.
  • Patch test on your inner arm if you have sensitive skin, and keep perfume away from your eyes.
  • Store bottles away from heat and sunlight, with the cap on.

Shop every oud perfume, all Arabian perfume and niche perfume, all 100% authentic and dispatched from the UK.

More people are switching to a natural shampoo: one built on plant-derived cleansers, with milks, waters and botanical extracts in place of a long list of synthetics. But "natural" is not a legal term in the UK, so the label alone tells you little. Here is how to read a shampoo, which one suits dry hair, frizz or a flaky scalp, and the conditioner or hair mask to follow it with.

What makes a shampoo "natural"?

Every shampoo needs a cleanser to lift oil and dirt. In the shampoos below, most come from coconut, corn or sugar beet: names such as decyl glucoside, coco-glucoside, sodium cocoyl isethionate and cocamidopropyl betaine. Around them sit the ingredients that give each shampoo its character, such as rice water, goat milk, rosemary or neem. Always read the full ingredient list on the product page: it tells you far more than the word "natural" on the front.

Shampoo for dry hair

Dry hair needs a cleanse that leaves moisture behind. Look for a creamy shampoo with milks, proteins or oils.

  • Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml): goat milk and jasmine flower water with hydrolysed keratin, pea protein, panthenol and jojoba oil, in a creamy lather. Vilvah makes it for dry, frizzy or chemically treated hair. Our goat milk soap guide covers Vilvah’s other goat milk products.
  • Deyga Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99, 50ml or 220ml): rice water with coconut- and corn-derived cleansers. A light, everyday shampoo for all hair types.

Rice water shampoo

Rice water has long been used in Asian hair care, where people rinsed their hair with the water left from soaking rice. A rice water shampoo puts that into an easy, everyday cleanser; the Deyga one leads its ingredient list with rice water and leaves hair feeling soft and smooth.

Shampoo for a flaky scalp

Scalp shampoos use herbal ingredients with a fresh, clean feel:

  • Vilvah Herbal Shampoo for Dandruff Control (from £12.99): neem leaf, tea tree and black pepper oils, rosemary and basil waters and amla, made without parabens.
  • Deyga Anti Dandruff Shampoo (£14.99, 220ml): rosemary leaf hydrosol, ginger extract and a yeast ferment extract, with mild cleansers. Deyga makes it for frequent use and says it is safe for colour-treated hair.

Massage it into the scalp, not just the lengths, and leave it for a minute before rinsing. Flakes, itching or redness that do not settle are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP. Shop every shampoo for dandruff, or see our dandruff care edit.

Conditioner for dry hair

Conditioner smooths the hair after shampoo, so it detangles easily and feels softer.

  • Vilvah Cream Conditioner (£15.99, 250ml): tucuma butter, broccoli seed oil, aloe vera, jasmine and pea protein. Vilvah says it can also be left on for up to 15 minutes as a mask.
  • Deyga Soy Milk Conditioner (£11.99, 50ml): soybean extract, argan oil, provitamin B5 and vitamin E in a lightweight texture.

Hair mask for dry hair

Once a week, swap your conditioner for a mask. Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99, 200g) combines goat milk with ceramides, argan oil, vitamin E and a seaweed extract. Apply it to clean, damp lengths, leave it for 10 to 15 minutes, then rinse. Vilvah says it also works as a leave-in styling aid for curls. See every hair mask for dry hair.

How to wash your hair

  1. Wet your hair thoroughly with warm, not hot, water.
  2. Use a coin-sized amount of shampoo, more for long or thick hair.
  3. Focus on the scalp, massaging with your fingertips, not your nails. The lather will clean the lengths as you rinse.
  4. Rinse well, then apply conditioner to the mid-lengths and ends.
  5. Leave it for a minute or two, comb through with a wide-tooth comb, and rinse.
  6. Pat dry with a towel rather than rubbing, which can rough up the hair.

How often? Dry or curly hair often does well with two or three washes a week; an oily scalp may prefer every other day. Natural shampoos can lather less than you are used to, so a second, smaller wash is fine.

Before and after the wash

Oiling before a wash is a long tradition in Indian hair care: read our guide to hair oils. For frizz after drying, a few drops of serum help smooth flyaways; the Vilvah Shampoo & Hair Serum Kit (£25.99) pairs the Goat Milk Shampoo with the Anti-Frizz Hair Serum. See all hair serums for frizzy hair.

Good to know

  • Patch test a new shampoo behind the ear, especially one with essential oils such as tea tree or rosemary.
  • Keep it out of your eyes; rinse with water if it gets in.
  • Switching brands? Give your hair two or three weeks to settle before you judge.

Shop every natural shampoo and the full haircare range, all dispatched from the UK.

Few perfumes have travelled by word of mouth like Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa. It belongs to a wave of Arabian perfume houses, from Lattafa and Afnan to Al Haramain, Arabiyat Prestige and Maison Alhambra, whose rich, warm scents have found a big following in the UK. Here is what is in Khamrah Qahwa, what makes a perfume "Arabian", and how to choose one.

What does Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa smell like?

"Qahwa" is the Arabic word for coffee, and that is the idea at the heart of Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa Eau de Parfum (£26.99, 100ml). Its notes, from top to base:

  • Top: cinnamon, cardamom and ginger, the spices of Arabic coffee.
  • Heart: praline, candied fruits and white flowers.
  • Base: coffee, vanilla, tonka bean, benzoin and musk.

So it opens spicy, turns sweet and nutty, and settles into coffee and vanilla. It is an amber-woody, gourmand scent made for men and women, and it suits cooler months and evenings best.

More from Lattafa

Lattafa perfume is known for warm, generous scents at friendly prices. Alongside Khamrah Qahwa, we list:

  • Lattafa Teriaq (£29.99): caramel, bitter almond, pink pepper and apricot, then honey, rhubarb and rose over leather, vanilla and musk. Unisex.
  • Lattafa Maahir Black Edition (£25.99): black and pink pepper with saffron, then labdanum and cade oil over leather, cedarwood, guaiac wood and patchouli. A darker, smoky choice.
  • Lattafa Yara Candy (£26.99): green mandarin and blackcurrant, a strawberry-candy and gardenia heart, and vanilla, musk and sandalwood. Made for women.

See every Lattafa scent on the Lattafa page.

Afnan, Arabiyat Prestige and Maison Alhambra

Afnan 9am Dive (£26.99) is the fresh one: lemon, mint, pink pepper and blackcurrant, then apple, incense and cedarwood. Afnan Supremacy Gold (£27.99) is warmer, with nutmeg, violet and peach blossom over amber, vanilla, oud and benzoin. More on the Afnan page.

Arabiyat Prestige Nyla (£25.99, 80ml) is a bright floral-fruity scent for women: coconut, peach and mandarin, then tiare, jasmine and rose over white musk. See Arabiyat Prestige. Maison Alhambra adds a wide range of floral, fruity and woody eau de parfums at friendly prices.

What makes a perfume "Arabian"?

There is no strict rule, but Arabian perfume usually leans on a few ingredients:

  • Oud (agarwood): a deep, woody, slightly smoky note.
  • Amber and resins such as benzoin and labdanum: warm and sweet.
  • Saffron, cardamom and cinnamon: spice.
  • Rose and musk: soft and rounded.

Most of the scents above are eau de parfum, which typically holds around 15–20% perfume oil. Read extrait vs eau de parfum for what each label means.

Arabian perfume in stock now

Warm and spicy

Al Haramain Amber Oud Tobacco Edition (£32.99, 60ml) shares Khamrah Qahwa's love of spice: tobacco leaf, cinnamon, black pepper and ginger, then vanilla, clove, star anise, cacao and tonka bean. Al Haramain Amber Oud Black Edition (£39.99) pairs cardamom and lavender with leather, amber and benzoin.

Sweet and fruity

Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition (from £32.99) is bergamot, melon and pineapple over vanilla and musk, a popular first Arabian perfume. Al Haramain Amber Oud Ruby Edition (from £41.99) mixes saffron and bitter almond with jasmine and ambergris. Al Haramain Amber Musk (£39.99) is softer: amber, musk, vanilla and resins.

Oud and saffron

Fumeri Oud Saffron (£29.99) and SAP Saffron Oud Extrait de Parfum (£43.99) both open on saffron and spice before oud, cedarwood and smoky woods, with amber, leather and musk. Montale Aoud Safran (£62.99) builds on saffron and oud with rose and amber.

Browse all Arabian perfume and oud perfume. For designer ouds such as Tom Ford Oud Wood and Gucci Intense Oud, read our oud perfume guide.

How to wear a rich, warm perfume

  • Start small: one or two sprays on the neck or wrists. You can add more; you cannot take it away.
  • Spray on moisturised skin, so the scent has something to sit on. We explain how in how to layer oud with body butter.
  • Try it on skin before you decide. Warm notes change over the first hour, so judge the base, not just the first spray.
  • Patch test if your skin is sensitive to fragrance.

Arabian perfume also makes a generous gift: see our Christmas gift guide.

In India, oiling your hair is a weekly ritual passed down through families: warm oil massaged into the scalp, left to soak in, then washed out. It is one of the simplest ways to make dry hair feel softer and look glossier, and it is easy to start. Here is what the classic ingredients (amla, bhringraj, castor oil and more) bring to a hair oil, how to choose one, and how to oil your hair step by step.

What does a hair oil do?

A hair oil coats the hair shaft, so lengths feel softer, smoother and less frizzy, and look shinier. Used before washing, it cushions the lengths so they feel less dry after shampoo. And the scalp massage that goes with it is relaxing in itself. Think of a hair oil as a conditioning treatment for hair and scalp.

The key ingredients, explained

  • Amla (Indian gooseberry, Emblica officinalis) is the best-known ingredient in Ayurvedic hair care. In an amla hair oil, the dried fruit is steeped in a base oil such as coconut. Our Indian skincare guide covers amla and other Indian ingredients.
  • Bhringraj (Eclipta prostrata) is a herb traditionally used in Indian hair oils, often alongside amla. Bhringraj oil is usually a herbal infusion rather than a pure oil.
  • Castor oil is thick and rich. On its own it can feel heavy, so it works best mixed with lighter oils, which is how you will find it in most blends.

Oud is one of the richest notes in perfumery: smoky, resinous and warm. Yet even a great oud perfume can fade sooner than you expect on dry skin. The fix is simple and costs very little: layer it over a body butter. Here is why it works, how to do it, and three pairings from our shelves to try.

Why fragrance lasts longer on moisturised skin

Perfume oils evaporate fastest from dry skin. A thin layer of butter or lotion gives the fragrance something to cling to, so it tends to unfold more slowly and stay closer to you for longer. Rich butters with cocoa, shea or almond oil work especially well under warm notes such as oud, amber and vanilla. If your skin runs dry, a body butter for dry skin does two jobs at once.

How to layer, step by step

  1. Shower first. Pat skin almost dry; slightly damp skin takes butter more evenly.
  2. Warm a little butter between your palms and press it into pulse points: wrists, inner elbows, the base of the neck and behind the knees.
  3. Wait a minute so the butter settles.
  4. Spray once or twice from about 15 cm onto the same spots. Don't rub your wrists together; let it dry.
  5. Top up the butter, not the perfume, later in the day if skin feels dry. The scent often comes back with it.

Three skin + scent pairings to try

1. Sweet and golden: Chocolate Body Butter + Amber Oud Gold

The Deyga Chocolate Body Butter is made with cocoa and nourishing oils and has a light chocolate scent. Under Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition, with its melon, pineapple, vanilla and musk, it reads as a soft gourmand. For more intensity, try the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait. "Chocolate body butter" and "Al Haramain Amber Oud" are both popular UK searches, and this is the pairing that shows why.

2. Floral and warm: Rose & Geranium Body Butter + Amber Oud Ruby

The Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter carries rose and geranium essential oils. Layer it under Al Haramain Amber Oud Ruby Edition, which opens with saffron and bitter almond over jasmine, cedarwood, ambergris and musk, and the florals meet in the middle. If you love rose with oud, Montale Aoud Damascus is another lovely match.

3. Clean and smoky: a light lotion + Gucci Intense Oud

Not every pairing needs a scented base. A light, quick-absorbing lotion such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion lets a dark scent like Gucci Intense Oud (black pepper, incense, woods, leather and an oud accord) lead the way, while still giving it something to hold on to. Want a luxury option? Try Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter.

Which base suits your skin?

If your skin is very dry, a rich butter such as Deyga's cocoa or rose formulas gives the most staying power. If you prefer something lighter in warm weather, a lotion like Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion absorbs faster and still helps the fragrance last. On sensitive days, keep the base unscented and let the perfume do the talking.

A few tips for oud

  • Less is more. Oud projects well; one or two sprays over butter usually lasts.
  • Spray clothes lightly, not silk, to keep a soft trail.
  • Match the mood. Sweet butters suit amber ouds, floral butters suit rose ouds, and neutral lotions suit smoky ouds.

New to oud and Arabian perfume? Our guide to Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa and Arabian perfume explains the notes and how to choose. For Tom Ford Oud Wood, Gucci Intense Oud and other designer ouds, see our oud perfume guide.
